preamble: Backing of the close-mid front rounded vowel [ø] to back [o], keeping height and rounding. Standard (Tashkent) Uzbek lost the Turkic front rounded vowels together with vowel harmony, so inherited *ö fell together with *o as /o/, spelled oʻ: oʻz /oz/ 'self' corresponds to Turkish öz. Ido (2025) measured the rounded vowels of a Tashkent speaker and found no backness difference between /bol/ 'divide!' (< Proto-Turkic *bȫl-) and /bol/ 'become!' (< *bōl-), although several descriptions still posit a front ö for the standard language. Many Uzbek dialects keep the front rounded vowels. Inherited *ü merged with /u/ in the same way (y → u).

examples.note: Ido (2025) uses oʻz as the key word for close-mid back /o/, against open-mid /ɔ/ in oz /ɔz/ 'few'.

Homophonous with boʻl- /bol/ 'become!' (< Proto-Turkic *bōl-). Ido's measurements give a mean F2 of 836 Hz for 'divide!' and 873 Hz for 'become!', both back; Boeschoten (1998), cited by Ido, had reported a contrast bol- 'become' vs böl- 'divide'.

examples.from: Chagatai سوز söz 'word' (< Proto-Turkic *söŕ; cf. Turkish söz)

examples.note: Wiktionary's narrow transcriptions show a slightly advanced [o̟], and central [ɵ] in koʻl [k̟ʰɵl] 'lake' and koʻk [kɵk] 'blue'; Ido (2025) places /o/ at the back of the vowel space. The fronted variants are not tied to old *ö: Wiktionary gives the same narrow transcription for boʻl- 'become' (< *bōl-) as for boʻl- 'divide', and Wikipedia writes boʻlib 'being' (< *bōl-) as [bɵˈlɪ̞p]. Proto-Turkic vowel length is lost in Uzbek.

sources: Ido, S. (2025). Uzbek. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 55(1–2), 152–168. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100324000148
